entries.en: What do you think, Commander? We won't be staying on Eden Prime too long, will we? I'm itching for some real action!
I sincerely hope you're kidding, Corporal. Your 'real action' usually ends with me patching up crew members in the infirmary.
I know how things work, Commander. I've seen my share of combat, but it's foolish to go looking for trouble.
You could both take a lesson from the captain. He's not afraid of combat, but he knows the value of restraint, too.
Yes, Commander? Is there something you need?
I've served with him for a few tours now. He knows when to let things slide and when to crack the whip.
The crew knows he's seen pretty much anything they'll ever run into. And he cares about the people under his command.
Turians are generally well-respected by the other species. Their fleet has more patrols protecting Citadel space than any other.
They don't always get on well with us, though. Some people find them too rigid. Others still blame them for the First Contact War.
As for Nihlus, I haven't said more than two words to him. He usually only speaks to the captain.
I hope we get a chance to see him in action. I heard Nihlus took down an entire enemy platoon all by himself!
Only what I've heard. Spectre agents work directly for the Citadel Council. They usually work alone or in small groups.
Spectres don't have any official power, though. Basically, they're a shadow organization with a mandate to preserve and protect galactic stability.
Protect it at any cost. Don't forget that part. Spectres operate above the law!
Goodbye, Commander.
Marines are meant to fight. You just fix us up when we're done.
What do you know about Captain Anderson?
What can you tell me about Nihlus?
What do you know about the Spectres?
How do you control agents with unlimited power?
The captain's waiting for me.
Part of the job, Doc.
Captain Anderson
Nihlus
The Spectres
Goodbye.
That's dangerous.
I enlisted right out of med school. Earth always seemed boring to me... too safe, too secure. I figured the colonies were teeming with exotic adventure.
I wanted to travel the stars, tending the wounds of tough soldiers with piercing eyes and sensitive souls. Turns out military life isn't quite as romantic as I'd imagined.
But humanity needs the Alliance if we want to keep expanding through the Traverse, and the Alliance always needs good doctors. So I stayed on to do my part.
Sometimes I think about opening a private practice back on Earth, or maybe taking a position at one of the new med centers out in the colonies.
But there's something special about working on soldiers. If I left the Alliance now, I'd feel like I was abandoning them.
I suppose the Council could revoke the Spectre status of an agent who got out of hand. At that point, Citadel Security Services would take over.
Those C-Sec grunts wouldn't stand a chance. A Spectre's worth twenty ordinary soldiers.
The corporal's confusing romantic legends with reality, Commander.
Spectres usually come from the Council races. Like the turians. We've been trying to get a human accepted into their ranks for years now. So far, it hasn't happened.
They're always getting dropped into impossible situations. Forced to survive unbeatable odds. Just like you on Akuze!
How did you end up serving on an Alliance ship?
Ever think you made the wrong choice?
Why don't we have any of our own people in there?
Personal questions
Any regrets?
There are no human Spectres?
I'd never worked with him before this mission. But he has an impressive service record. Over a dozen special commendations.
Tends to keep to himself, though. Maybe because of the headaches. It's not easy being an L2.
Well, most biotics now use the L3 implants. Lt. Alenko was wired with the old L2 configuration. Sometimes there are complications.
You're lucky, Commander. Your implants use the L3 configuration. Lt. Alenko has the older L2. Far more complications.
How well do you know the lieutenant?
What does that have to do with it?
Kaidan Alenko
An L2?
Hey, Commander! You'd make a good Spectre!
Sorry, Commander. I-- I didn't mean to offend you. I respect what you did there. We all do.
Let's not dwell on the past, Commander. Was there something else you needed?
You're a war hero, right? Held off an entire enemy fleet during the Blitz single-handed. That's the kind of talent the Spectres are looking for.
This is all just wild speculation. The Spectres aren't interested in recruiting humans. No matter how capable.
What you did on Torfan. That's what they're looking for. Success at any cost. Ruthless efficiency. Show no mercy.
No! I didn't mean.... Sorry, Commander. That just came out wrong. I never meant any disrespect.
Fifty marines died there, Jenkins.
I try not to think about Akuze.
I didn't enjoy Torfan. I just did what I had to do.
Sounds like my kind of job.
Show some respect!
Those are bad memories.
I'm not a monster!
I could do that.
The crew's lives are in your hands, Shepard. Try to take good care of them.
I'm glad to see you're feeling better, Commander.
Yes, Commander? Is there something you need?
Severe mental disabilities, insanity, crippling physical pain. There's a long list of horrific side effects. Kaidan's lucky. He just gets migraines.
What kind of complications?
Complications?
It's strange, being a fugitive from the Alliance.
This crew has sacrificed everything for you, Shepard. Don't let us down.
The asari are remarkable, aren't they? Can you believe Liara is twice my age?
Sorry, Doc. But this waiting's killing me. I've never been on a mission like this before. Not one with a Spectre on board!
Sorry, Commander. But this waiting's killing me. I've never been on a mission like this before. Not one with a Spectre on board!
Easy for you to say. You proved yourself on Akuze. Everybody knows what you can do.
Easy for you to say. You proved yourself in the Blitz. Everybody knows what you can do.
Easy for you to say. You proved yourself on Torfan. Everybody knows what you can do.
This is my big chance. I need to show the brass what I can do!
Don't worry, ma'am. I'm not going to screw this up.
Don't worry, sir. I'm not going to screw this up.
It's very peaceful, Commander. They've been real careful with development, so you don't have any city noise or pollution.
My parents lived on the outskirts of the colony. At night, I used to climb this big hill and stare across the fields back at the lights from the main settlement.
It was gorgeous. But when I got older, I realized it was a little too calm and quiet for me. That's why I joined the Alliance. Even paradise gets boring after a while.
Not really sure, Commander. Eden Prime's one of our most stable colonies. Good place to take the Normandy for her shakedown run, I guess. No real danger there.
But there's got to be something else going on. We've got a Spectre on board! That's why I'm so wound up. I can't wait for the real mission to start!
I heard Nihlus once took down an entire enemy platoon all by himself. Man, I can't believe I'm on a mission with an actual Spectre!
The Spectres police themselves. An agent goes rogue, they send another agent to take 'em down. That's Spectre justice!
I should go.
You need to calm down, Corporal. A good soldier stays cool, even under fire.
Only a fool goes looking for a fight, Corporal.
Just treat this like every other assignment you've had and everything will work out.
Do your job, follow my orders, and there won't be any problems.
You're young, Corporal. You have a long career ahead of you. Don't do something stupid to mess it up.
This mission isn't about personal glory, Corporal! We have a job to do. Don't do anything stupid to mess it up!
You're from Eden Prime, aren't you Jenkins? What's it like?
Any idea why Eden Prime was chosen as our destination?
Goodbye.
Relax, Jenkins.
The doctor's right.
You'll do fine.
It's just another mission.
There's no rush.
Be careful.
Don't play the hero!
Eden Prime
Why are we going there?
Spectres sound dangerous.
Spectres sound dangerous.
Spectres sound dangerous.
Spectres sound dangerous.
